```{r}
#| label: setup
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(classInt)

# Number of classes for each map
n_equal <- 5
n_jenks <- 5

# Equal Earth projection (equal-area, suited to choropleths)
crs_map <- "+proj=eqearth +lon_0=0"
```

## Data and boundaries

Data: *Women's Political Empowerment Index* (0 = lowest, 1 = highest), Our World in Data, 2025.
Boundaries: Natural Earth via `rnaturalearth`. Countries are joined by ISO-3 code, with fixes for
codes that Natural Earth leaves blank (France, Norway) or that OWID defines itself (Kosovo, `OWID_KOS`).
Countries without data are shown in grey.

```{r}
#| label: data
dat <- read_csv("Data/OurWinData2026-women-political-empowerment-index.csv",
                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(index = `Women's Political Empowerment Index`,
         region = `World region according to OWID`)

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") |>
  filter(adm0_a3 != "ATA") |>                       # Antarctica is not a country
  mutate(Code = case_when(
    adm0_a3 == "KOS"                ~ "OWID_KOS",    # Kosovo
    adm0_a3 %in% c("IOA", "ATC")    ~ NA_character_, # Australian external territories
    TRUE                            ~ iso_a3_eh      # fixes France / Norway
  )) |>
  left_join(dat, by = "Code") |>
  st_transform(crs_map)

# Sanity check: every country in the data set is on the map
stopifnot(all(dat$Code %in% world$Code))
cat(nrow(dat), "countries with data;",
    sum(is.na(world$index)), "map units without data (grey)\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
# Build class labels from break values; classes use the exact breaks
classify <- function(x, breaks, digits = 2) {
  lab <- paste0(formatC(head(breaks, -1), format = "f", digits = digits), " to ",
                formatC(tail(breaks, -1), format = "f", digits = digits))
  factor(cut(x, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = lab), levels = lab)
}

# Small countries are invisible at world scale: add a marker so all are represented
small <- world |>
  filter(!is.na(index), as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) < 2.5e10) |>   # < 25,000 km²
  st_point_on_surface()

map_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),   # white oceans
        legend.position  = "bottom",
        legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.caption     = element_text(colour = "grey35", hjust = 0))

make_map <- function(fills, title, subtitle, legend_title) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = world, aes(fill = cls), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = small, aes(fill = cls), shape = 21, size = 1.6,
            colour = "grey25", stroke = 0.25, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills, na.value = "grey80", drop = FALSE,
                      name = legend_title, na.translate = TRUE,
                      labels = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "No data", x),
                      guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top",
                                           override.aes = list(colour = "grey40"))) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
         caption = "Source: Our World in Data, Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025. Boundaries: Natural Earth.") +
    map_theme
}
```

## Map 1 — Equal intervals, single purple hue

Classes of equal width across the observed range; lightness of one hue encodes the level.

```{r}
#| label: map-equal
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, five equal-interval classes in a light-to-dark purple scale. Countries without data are grey."
br_equal <- seq(min(dat$index), max(dat$index), length.out = n_equal + 1)
world$cls <- classify(world$index, br_equal)
small$cls <- classify(small$index, br_equal)

purples <- c("#f2f0f7", "#cbc9e2", "#9e9ac8", "#756bb1", "#54278f")

make_map(purples,
         "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
         "Equal-interval classes, sequential purple scale",
         "Index (0 to 1)")
```

## Map 2 — Jenks natural breaks, a different hue for each level

Jenks breaks minimise within-class variance, so class limits follow gaps in the data.
A diverging, colour-blind-safe palette gives each level its own hue (red → yellow → blue).

```{r}
#| label: map-jenks
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025, five Jenks natural-break classes shown in distinct hues from red (lowest) through yellow to blue (highest). Countries without data are grey."
br_jenks <- classIntervals(dat$index, n = n_jenks, style = "jenks")$brks
world$cls <- classify(world$index, br_jenks)
small$cls <- classify(small$index, br_jenks)

hues <- c("#d7191c", "#fdae61", "#ffffbf", "#abd9e9", "#2c7bb6")   # RdYlBu, 5 classes

make_map(hues,
         "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
         "Jenks natural breaks, distinct hue per level",
         "Index (0 to 1)")
```

### With bad selection of hues

```{r}
#| label: map-jenks-Qualitative
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "World choropleth map of the Women's Political Empowerment Index in 2025."
br_jenks <- classIntervals(dat$index, n = n_jenks, style = "jenks")$brks
world$cls <- classify(world$index, br_jenks)
small$cls <- classify(small$index, br_jenks)

hues <- c('#377eb8', '#984ea3', '#4daf4a',"#ffff33", "#a65628")  #  5 classes




make_map(hues,
         "Women's Political Empowerment Index, 2025",
         "Jenks natural breaks, Qualitative palette",
         "Index (0 to 1)")
```

## Class breaks and counts

```{r}
#| label: breaks
tibble(
  method = rep(c("Equal interval", "Jenks"), each = n_equal),
  class  = c(levels(classify(dat$index, br_equal)),
             levels(classify(dat$index, br_jenks))),
  countries = c(table(classify(dat$index, br_equal)),
                table(classify(dat$index, br_jenks)))
) |> knitr::kable()
```
